question: Do the order-3 marginal emission columns (He7 k3k4/144 + He9 k3^3/1296 + He5 closure-k5/120) own the per-step mean bias?
method: oracle-state per-layer computation (rank 35, mc_oracle_deep + second_order taps): order-3 post-mean shift magnitude vs measured model-minus-oracle pre-mean error; per-unit correlation of the W-pushed prediction with the next-layer error

numbers.order3_net_rel_rms_per_layer: 1.1e-6 (L2) to 7.5e-6 (L14); k5-free and k5 halves partially cancel (net < either)
numbers.measured_pre_mean_err_rel: 1.8-2.3e-4, roughly FLAT with depth and near the 8M-MC noise floor (se 1.1-3.5e-4) - per-layer increments are below per-layer MC resolution

reframe: The L16 mean-channel error (~2e-4 relative, = the whole residual) is the accumulated echo of per-layer k3/k4 STATE errors, not a marginal-density truncation: teacher-forcing true k3/k4 at every layer reaches 8.2e-9 (~0.9e-4 relative), and the L16 attribution's small k4 share (0.05) measures only the LAST-layer delta, not the trajectory echo. Corollary: trajectory-COHERENT state repair (all channels together, every layer - like the K22 supply, -60%) is the mechanism that moves the mean channel; single-channel partials perturb the co-adapted trajectory and lose (5 receipts).
